A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ELMUR, with clearly matching architecture, theory, experiments, and authors. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original T-Maze, POPGym, MIKASA-Robo, and CartPole experiments, including memory-component and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds D4RL control, ViZDoom navigation, broader robotics evaluation, and memory-probing results.

M1.justification: The architecture, memory updates, cross-attention, MoE components, and supervised losses remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 adds a tested input adaptation conditioning ELMUR on returns-to-go, observations, and actions, alongside its original observation-only mode.

E1.justification: v2 expands MIKASA-Robo evaluation from four tasks to 32, adding ShellGame, interception, rotation, shape-recall, and multi-color task families. It also adds high-dimensional D4RL locomotion tasks and ViZDoom-Two-Colors navigation with visual cue recall. The original benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Trajectory Transformer becomes an additional reported comparator in v2 Table 4. The original comparison sets remain intact. RATE, RMT, TrXL, and the other ViZDoom comparators already appeared in v1 experiments; their use on an added benchmark does not independently establish new baseline methods.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings and the shared hyperparameter table are retained. New protocols include normalized D4RL evaluation under two conditioning modes and post-hoc memory probing: collecting 1,000 episodes, retaining successful episodes, training separate probes by layer and timestep, and using an 80/20 training-validation split. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: The original component and hyperparameter ablations remain unchanged. v2 adds conditioning comparisons and extensive analyses of memory content and operation: color decoding, slot updates, cosine similarity, embedding variance, PCA trajectories, and read/write attention maps (Appendices A.5 and A.9–A.11).

E5.justification: The original three-run protocol, four-run T-Maze exception, SEM reporting, and Figure 5 confidence intervals are retained. v2 additionally specifies six runs with SEM for ViZDoom and averaging across 20 batches with standard-deviation shading in Figure 11. These are new reporting details for added analyses, not increases established for existing experiments.

E6.justification: Shared main results and the full POPGym table remain unchanged. Added results include D4RL averages of 76.4 and 74.7 under different conditioning modes, ViZDoom returns of 55.28±0.94 for ELMUR versus 59.21±1.19 for RATE, and 32-task robotics sums of 9.24 versus 5.42. Memory probes also add evidence of target-color decodability.

T1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A.1–A.3 retain the exponential-forgetting result, half-life and retention-horizon expressions, boundedness assumptions and proof, and memory-intensive-environment definition. No substantive mathematical revision is evident.

C1.justification: The architecture, theoretical contributions, and million-step retention claims are retained. The abstract and introduction expand the robotics claim to approximately 70% aggregate improvement and wins on 21 of 23 tasks. The aggregate comparison is supported, but Table 8 shows only 18 highest means among the 23 tasks with nonzero scores.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretations concerning conditioning robustness, navigation applicability, stable color representations, slot allocation, and layer/head specialization. Appendices A.9–A.11 further attribute performance causally to functional memory rather than parameter count, exceeding what the post-hoc analyses alone establish. The original limitations paragraph is retained in A.12.

D1.justification: v2 documents the probes' three-layer, 512-hidden-unit MLP, Adam optimization, and 200 training epochs. A new reproducibility statement reports supplementary implementation, training scripts, and configuration files. The original policy hyperparameters, demonstration counts, hardware disclosure, and project address are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Trajectory Transformer, ViZDoom, MuJoCo, and PCA, and removes the RozumFormer/Staroverov reference. The broad positioning against recurrent models, external-memory architectures, and robotic transformers remains stable. The updated Cherepanov conference references correspond to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are preserved. v2 updates the title, affiliations, and conference header, adds a reproducibility statement, and inserts new appendix sections while renumbering retained material. The revision primarily adds scientific content rather than extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds three substantive result tables for D4RL, ViZDoom, and the full robotics suite, plus Figures 8–15 showing the navigation environment and memory analyses. Existing tables are renumbered and repositioned, with revised highlighting and page flow; the original main figures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v1's robotics evidence covered four tasks, and its fully observable check saturated CartPole. v2 substantially strengthens validation through the full robotics suite, harder control and visual-navigation tasks, and probes demonstrating stored target-color information. The added results expose failures as well as successes, making applicability more assessable. These gains outweigh the new reporting and interpretation weaknesses, although the unsupported 21/23 win count and causal claims based on observational probing need correction.
